conflicts.fact: Coordinate rule for reflection in y = −x
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 states reflection in y = −x maps (a, b) → (−b, −a). Lesson 8 says a table of 'all six coordinate reflection rules studied across Lessons 3–6' is provided, but Lessons 3–6 only cover four mirror lines (x-axis, y-axis, y = x, y = −x). The count of rules is inconsistent.

conflicts.fact: Where the mirror line lies relative to the object and image / what the mirror surface is
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the matatu mirror 'acts as a mirror line' and that fold lines equal mirror lines, but treats the lorry image as the same size. Lesson 2 says the mirror surface acts as a line of symmetry dividing the 'lorry + image' system into two congruent halves, and claims this is WHY the image looks identical (the mirror line guarantees congruence), which contradicts Lesson 1's framing of congruence as the unresolved puzzle and later lessons' proof that congruence follows from distance preservation.

conflicts.fact: What Lesson 2 established, as recalled by Lesson 3
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says that in Lessons 1 and 2 learners discovered by mirrors and folding that the image is equidistant and the joining segment is perpendicular to the mirror line. Lesson 2 only finds lines of symmetry in shapes and does not investigate equidistance or perpendicularity; Lesson 4 presents these as discoveries made for the first time. Lesson 3 also says the Lesson 2 model had arrows showing equal distances and perpendicularity, but Lesson 2's model has only a mirror line, 'congruent half' arrows and a table.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson's model/previous content is referenced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 teacher says Lesson 1 added lines of symmetry, Lesson 2 added the concept of reflection, and Lesson 3 coordinate rules. Lesson 7 tells learners to 'Open your cumulative model from Lesson 3' and describes it as a Cartesian plane diagram built since Lesson 1, while Lesson 1's model was a simple diagram of a mirror and shape with no Cartesian plane.

Lesson 1's model is a diagram with object, mirror line, image and labels. Lesson 6 says the cumulative model since Lesson 1 shows 'labels for the four properties of reflection', which in Lesson 4 were discovered, and Lesson 4 says the cumulative class diagram was started in Lesson 1 as an A3 poster, while Lesson 1 describes only individual exercise book models.

conflicts.fact: Direct vs opposite congruence of triangles from the same template
conflicts.versions: The phenomenon says triangles cut from one template can sometimes be flipped onto each other (direct) and sometimes not (opposite). Lesson 7 claims the construction tests each produce a unique triangle 'up to orientation' but in Observed says reflection always gives opposite congruence 'because reflection reverses orientation', and claims the lorry and image 'cannot be superimposed without flipping', while Lesson 4 shows folding tracing paper makes object and image coincide exactly (which is a flip, consistent) but Lesson 2 describes the halves as matching by folding as 'direct'; the usage of direct/opposite is inconsistent across lessons.
